title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
summary: Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho, and Yoshua Bengio submitted 'Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate' on September 1, 2014. The paper proposed extending encoder-decoder neural machine translation by allowing the model to automatically soft-search for source-sentence parts relevant to predicting each target word rather than relying only on a single fixed-length source representation.
significance: A documented neural-machine-translation research milestone for learned soft alignment/attention in sequence models, addressing the fixed-length-vector bottleneck in encoder-decoder translation.

verification.note: The original arXiv record establishes the September 1, 2014 first-submission date, authors, and the proposed soft-search/alignment mechanism for neural machine translation.
